hints: Focus on what counts as a strong organic base in AS Chemistry, think of the alkoxide ion $\text{RO}^-$ rather than $\text{OH}^-$.
Recall how ethanol behaves as a very weak acid, so look for the reaction where its $\text{O-H}$ bond is broken by a very reactive metal.
Compare oxidation, dehydration and substitution of ethanol with the metal-acid type reaction, and see which one leaves an $\text{O}^-$ attached to the ethyl group.
walkthrough:
**What is a strong organic base?**

Think of the cousin of $\text{NaOH}$. If you replace $\text{H}$ in $\text{OH}^-$ with an alkyl group you get an alkoxide, $\text{RO}^-$. A classic example is sodium ethoxide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+$.

Key idea:
$$\text{R-OH} \rightarrow \text{R-O}^- + \text{H}^+ \text{ (removed)}$$

**Sort the four ethanol reactions**

Recall your ethanol reaction map. Acidified dichromate oxidises, hot aluminium oxide dehydrates, HCl substitutes, but sodium reacts as an acid-metal reaction.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{hot Al}_2\text{O}_3} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Write the sodium reaction and decide**

Sodium is strong enough to remove the hydroxyl proton from ethanol, just like with water but more slowly. This gives hydrogen gas and the alkoxide salt.

$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2$$
The product, sodium ethoxide, contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-$ ion which is a strong organic base.

options.A: Acidified sodium dichromate is an oxidising agent. It oxidises ethanol first to ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, then to ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. These are a neutral aldehyde and a weak acid, not a strong base.
options.B: Hot aluminium oxide acts as a dehydrating catalyst. It removes water from ethanol to form ethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$, an alkene. This is an elimination reaction and no basic alkoxide is formed.
options.C: Sodium reacts with the slightly acidic $\text{O-H}$ group of ethanol to form sodium ethoxide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{ONa}$, plus hydrogen. The ethoxide ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-$, is a strong organic base, analogous to $\text{OH}^-$.
options.D: Hydrogen chloride reacts by nucleophilic substitution of the $\text{-OH}$ group. It forms chloroethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, plus water. Chloroethane is a neutral halogenoalkane, not a base.
